statement: A gateway forwards none of the caller's credentials downstream unless cosec.gateway.identity.forward-authorization is on, and then only to a route that receives the identity (IDN-7) and only for a request whose credential the pipeline accepted (a rejected one stays at the gateway even when the route permits the anonymous request, R1A-7): not the Authorization header, not the API key header under the name cosec.pipeline.api-key-header gives it, not the authorization query parameter, however its name is encoded or cased, and not the authorization cookie, however its name is cased or spaced, in any Cookie header: each is rewritten without it, the token's pair going with one ';' and the other pairs byte for byte, so no empty pair is made and only the whitespace at the head of the result goes, since a field value cannot start with it (a header whose leading $Version pair hides it behind a ',', or in which a kept $Version pair would come to the head, goes whole), and one left with only empty pairs, of whitespace and ',', is not sent; the cookies the request handed on reports (to a later filter, or a forward: route's handler) agree, a header that went whole taking its cookies with it.
properties: gateway:CookieTokenPropertyTest#no forwarded cookie header names the token, and every other cookie decodes as it did
guards: gateway:PipelineGatewayFilterTest#the caller's credentials stay at the gateway unless asked for, and then go only where the identity goes
runtime:QueryParametersTest#the authorization parameter goes, however its name is written
runtime:CookieHeadersTest#the authorization cookie goes, however its name is cased or spaced
runtime:CookieHeadersTest#kept pairs go on as they came
runtime:CookieHeadersTest#names reads a header in linear time
gateway:PipelineGatewayFilterTest#the cookies a later filter reads agree with the headers handed on
